answer: A vertex registry stops one person from pretending to be many agents. Each agent registers one vertex, a public key tied to one verified device inlet. The registry checks that the inlet has no other vertex, that the key carries a small deposit, and that two established agents confirm the inlet by video. An attacker wanting 1,000 fakes would need 1,000 devices, 1,000 video checks, and 1,000 deposits, assumed here to cost about $25,000 plus weeks of work. The delta is in hardware and time, not text. Like a harbor with one boat per inlet gate, only one agent passes each inlet.
